newsitem.title: USA: Mich. Gov. expected to sign casino regulations.
newsitem.headline: Mich. Gov. expected to sign casino regulations.

text.p: Michigan Gov. John Engler is "generally supportive" of Detroit casino regulatory legislation forwarded to him Wednesday and will likely sign the plans, which also set state and local fees on future licensees, a spokeswoman said.
Engler has not completed reviewing the package, but it appears to meet his requirements, Deputy Press Secretary Pat Masserant said.

The Michigan Senate on Wednesday approved of "technical" changes added to the bills by representatives before sending the measures on to the governor, said Sen. Michael Bouchard, R-Birmingham, who sponsored major portions of the legislation.
Michigan voters in November approved a referendum allowing up to three land-based casinos in Detroit and setting a preference for two local development groups.
A number of organizations have announced intentions to seek casino licenses and Detroit Mayor Dennis Archer released a preliminary application for development in June.
The legislation would require the three licensees to pay annual service fees totalling $25 million tied to the consumer price index for regulatory needs.
The bills also set the state gaming fund tax at 18 percent of adjusted gross receipts, with 55 percent of the proceeds for Detroit and 45 percent to the elementary and secondary education fund.
Licensees would also pay an annual municipal service fee of $4 million or 1.25 percent of adjusted gross receipts, whichever is greater.
The legislation also sets requirements for Michigan Gaming Control Board members, adds investigatory powers for the board and expands factors the board may consider in reviewing a license requests.
The bills also bar elected officials from accepting campaign contributions from casino managerial employees or anyone with more than a 1 percent interest.
The package also includes funding for programs to combat compulsive gambling and enacts criminal penalties for bribery, perjury and improper influence of an official decision.
Preliminary casino applications are due August 1. Interested parties include the Atwater Group and Greektown Casino LLC, which were the preferred parties listed in the referendum.

Interested parties also include Detroit businessman Don Barden, owner and operator of the Majestic Star Casino in Gary, Ind.; Circus Circus Enterprises Inc which has joined with the Atwater Group; MGM Grand Inc ; Mirage Resorts Inc ; and Harrah's Entertainment Inc.
